write 10 line assembly code to print hello world

Sure! Here's a 10-line x86-64 assembly program for Linux using NASM syntax that prints "Hello, World!" to the console:

```asm
section .data
    msg db 'Hello, World!', 0xA

section .text
    global _start

_start:
    mov rax, 1          ; sys_write system call
    mov rdi, 1          ; file descriptor (stdout)
    mov rsi, msg        ; message to write
    mov rdx, 14         ; message length
    syscall

    mov rax, 60         ; sys_exit
    mov rdi, 0          ; exit status
    syscall
```

### How to assemble and run (on Linux):
```bash
nasm -f elf64 helloworld.asm -o helloworld.o
ld helloworld.o -o helloworld
./helloworld
```

This will print:  
```
Hello, World!
```
